newsitem.title: USA: Weekly jobless claims jump in latest week.
newsitem.headline: Weekly jobless claims jump in latest week.

text.p: The number of Americans entering unemployment lines for the first time jumped by 19,000 last week, the government said on Thursday.

Despite the Memorial Day holiday, which shortened the period during which workers were able to apply for jobless benefits last week, the Labour Department reported that initial claims rose to 337,000 in the week ended May 31.
That figure compared with downwardly revised claims of 318,000 the week before and was the highest level for initial filings since the week ended May 3, when claims reached 348,000.
Wall Street economists had forecast initial jobless claims of 320,000 in the latest week.
The four-week moving average, which is usually considered a more accurate gauge because it smooths out weekly swings in the data, fell to 323,750 from a downwardly revised 326,000 the week before.
The four-week moving average was at its lowest level since the week ended April 19, when it stood at 321,750, the department said.
Four states reported decreases in claims exceeding 1,000 on an unadjusted basis in the week ended May 24, the latest period for which that data are available.
They were Ohio,with 1,903 fewer initial claims, Louisiana with 1,876, Kentucky with 1,849 and Tennessee with 1,425.

Louisiana said it had fewer layoffs in the transportation equipment industry. Tennessee reported fewer layoffs in manufacturing and in various industry categories, including lumber, apparel, leather goods, industrial machinery, service, and stone, clay and glass.
Ohio and Kentucky had no comment on claims activity.
Three states reported increases in claims exceeding 1,000, unadjusted, in the May 24 week.
They were Wisconsin with 1,061 additional claims filings, North Carolina with 1,037 and Georgia with 1,021.

Wisconsin said it had layoffs in construction, trade and service industries, and in manufacturing. North Carolina reported layoffs in the furniture industry, while Georgia said it had layoffs in the manufacturing sector.
